solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: School principal’s dreams involved with thesis

indicators.note: things that are involved are tangled together, so the letters get mixed up into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A school head's dreams are tangled up with the thesis she is writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay; all twelve letters of the two words are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A headmistress is the woman in charge of a school, its principal teacher and leader.

clue.text: Oriental barge finally at the rear of vessel

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word before it, so only its closing letter is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of barge
astern means towards or at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: An Eastern barge, with something happening at the back of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: E plus ASTERN gives EASTERN; 'at the rear of vessel' is one nautical word, not a placement instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and Eastern are synonyms, both describing things from Asia or the East.

clue.text: Resolution to put off motorway race

blocks.note: to deter is to discourage or put someone off
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, with the 1 read as the letter I
a race is a people, a nation

explanation.surface: A resolution passed to stop a race being held on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; setters write it MI, treating the digit 1 as a letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolution and determination are synonyms meaning firmness of purpose and resolve.

clue.text: Popular team serving porridge

blocks.note: something popular is in
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A well-liked group of staff dishing out porridge at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, so serving porridge means doing time.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside is slang for being locked up in jail, which is what doing a prison stretch involves.

clue.text: Touchy male parent met at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and lost, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prickly father whom someone met on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male parent' looks like a roundabout way to write FATHER or DAD, but the words themselves are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Touchy and temperamental both describe someone moody, easily upset and quick to take offence.

clue.text: Message from the Spanish about a month in France

indicators.note: about means around, so one part is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
mai is the French name for May

explanation.surface: A note sent from Spain about a month spent in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Message' sits at the front as the definition; the rest is two foreign words, one placed inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: An email is an electronic message sent between computers over the internet.

clue.text: Crooked lawyer seems hysterical at heart

indicators.note: at heart means inside, so the letters lie within the run of words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and into the second

explanation.surface: A dishonest lawyer who appears to be hysterical deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer starts with the last letter of 'seems' and continues into 'hysterical'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is a slang term for an unscrupulous, dishonest practitioner of law.

clue.text: Pass exams at last in Roman way

indicators.note: at last points to the final position, so only the closing letter is used
in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: via is Latin for road or way
the last letter of exams

explanation.surface: Passing exams finally, in the way the Romans did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass exams' reads as one phrase, but 'Pass' alone is the definition, meaning a travel permit.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official document or stamp that permits entry to a country, a kind of travel permit.

clue.text: Subsidiary picture of fashionable group

blocks.note: what is fashionable is in
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A smaller photograph of a trendy crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'of' joins definition and wordplay rather than signalling possession.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small image placed within a larger one, such as a detail map in the corner of a page.

clue.text: Brief account of problem by quite contrary girl

indicators.note: by means next to, so one part sits beside the other

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
the nursery rhyme begins 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary'

explanation.surface: A short report on the trouble caused by an awkward girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The contrary girl comes from the nursery rhyme 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary, how does your garden grow?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A summary is a short statement of the main points, a condensed account of something longer.

clue.text: Declared a retired minister leftist

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
Rev is short for Reverend, a minister of religion
a Red is a communist or left-winger

explanation.surface: A former minister announced that he was left-wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like it describes a minister no longer working, but it turns REV round.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly, so averred is a past-tense synonym of declared or asserted.

clue.text: Brilliant effect initially conveyed in story from the East

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter only
in an across answer, coming from the east means travelling right to left, backwards
in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: a tale is a story
the first letter of conveyed

explanation.surface: A dazzling result first conveyed in an Oriental tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the East' sounds like the story is Oriental, but it tells you to read the story's letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat, borrowed from French, means brilliant display or conspicuous success that wins acclaim.

clue.text: Learned person and I had returned in flat-bottomed boat

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the letters run backwards
in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: a punt is a flat-bottomed river boat pushed with a pole
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A scholar and I came back in a punt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I had' contracts to I'D, which is turned round and placed inside the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pundit is an expert or authority on a subject; the word comes from the Hindi for a scholar.

clue.text: Saw someone wandering around in lead

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for the metal lead
a rover is a person who roams about

explanation.surface: Spotted a person ambling about with a dog on its lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past-tense verb but is the noun meaning an old saying; 'lead' is the metal, not a leash.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, so it is a synonym for a proverb.

clue.text: Comparatively affected holiday-maker

blocks.note: first meaning: the comparative of camp, theatrically exaggerated
second meaning: someone staying in a tent or caravan

explanation.walkthrough: Camp means affected or showy in manner, and the comparative form adds -ER.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both the comparative of the adjective camp and the noun for a person holidaying under canvas.

clue.text: Field cut below apartment?

indicators.note: in a down answer, below means placed underneath, so one part follows the other

blocks.note: pad is slang for a flat or home
to dock is to cut or shorten

explanation.surface: A patch of grass mown beneath a block of flats.
explanation.walkthrough: Pad is informal for someone's flat, and dock means to cut, as with a tail or wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddock is a small enclosed field, usually for keeping horses.

clue.text: Evaluate a couple of ships rounding point

indicators.note: to round something is to go all the way about it, so one part encloses another

blocks.note: taken as written
SS stands for steamship, so two of them give two pairs
E for East, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Judging a pair of vessels as they sail round a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: A point is a compass point, here E; the pair of SS abbreviations sits either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to judge the worth or quality of something, a synonym of evaluate.

clue.text: Greek character immersed in home game

indicators.note: immersed in means sunk inside, so the letters lie within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from inside the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A Greek player wholly absorbed in a match on home turf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person, but here it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, and a character is a written letter.

clue.text: Welshman’s vehicle in centre of Oswestry

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another
the centre is the middle, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: the two middle letters of the eight-letter word
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A Welshman's car parked in the middle of Oswestry, a town on the Welsh border.
explanation.walkthrough: Oswestry is a market town in Shropshire close to Wales; its central pair of letters wraps the vehicle. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Evans is one of the most common Welsh surnames, so it stands for a typical man from Wales.

clue.text: Thin tip of lead in transmitter?

indicators.note: the tip is the very end point, here the opening letter
in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: a transmitter sends signals, so it is a sender
the first letter of lead

explanation.surface: A fine-pointed pencil lead used in some kind of transmitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip of lead' sounds like a pencil point, but it just means the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender and thin are synonyms describing something narrow or slight in width.

clue.text: Estimate speed

blocks.note: first meaning: to judge or value something
second meaning: pace

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the two words look like an instruction to guess a speed; they are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to judge or value; as a noun it means the pace at which something moves.

clue.text: Hard to catch four aboard English vessel

indicators.note: something aboard is carried inside, so one part is held within another

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a vase is a vessel for flowers
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people on an English ship are proving difficult to catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, since things go aboard, but here it is a container for flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasive describes someone or something that avoids capture, slipping away and dodging pursuit.

clue.text: Start of terrible drubbing? Something fishy here

indicators.note: the start is the beginning, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of terrible
a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: The beginnings of a heavy defeat, with a suspicion that something dodgy is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishy' suggests something suspicious, but the definition is literal: the answer is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater fish, so it is literally a fishy thing.

clue.text: Organised transport I appreciate crossing loch

indicators.note: to cross is to span over something, so one part lies across and around another

blocks.note: a bus is a form of transport
taken as written
to like something is to appreciate it
Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake

explanation.surface: Someone thanks the organisers of their trip across a Scottish loch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' looks like it describes the transport, but it is the definition. Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake, so the loch here is its name alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Businesslike means efficient, practical and systematic, much the same as organised.
